content.title: Mean, Median, Mode, Range, and Interquartile Range
content.overview: This lesson covers the core statistics used to describe the characteristics of one-variable data sets. We will learn how to calculate and interpret measures of center (mean, median, mode) and measures of spread (range, interquartile range).
learning_objectives: Calculate and interpret the arithmetic average (mean) of a data set.
Determine the median of an ordered data set.
Identify the value that appears most frequently in a data set (mode).
Calculate the difference between the maximum and minimum values (range).
Calculate the difference between the third and first quartiles (interquartile range).

sections.title: Measures of Center: Mean, Median, and Mode
sections.content:
Measures of center describe the 'middle' of the data. 1. **Mean**: The sum of all values divided by the total number of values. The formula is: Mean = $(\sum x) / n$. 2. **Median**: The middle value when the data is arranged in order from least to greatest. If there is an odd number of values, the median is the middle number; if there is an even number, the median is the average of the two middle numbers. 3. **Mode**: The value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set can have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.

![Steps to Calculate the Median](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/578115db-fbd5-422c-845e-af2143c1bfff-1786502063914-964.webp)

sections.title: Measures of Spread: Range and Interquartile Range (IQR)
sections.content: Measures of spread describe the variability of the data. 1. **Range**: The maximum value minus the minimum value. It reflects the total span of the data. 2. **Interquartile Range (IQR)**: The difference between the third quartile ($Q_3$) and the first quartile ($Q_1$), calculated as $IQR = Q_3 - Q_1$. $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half of the data, and $Q_3$ is the median of the upper half of the data. The IQR reflects the spread of the middle 50% of the data and is not sensitive to outliers.

worked_examples.question: Given the data set: 3, 7, 10, 14, 16. Find the mean and median of this data set.
worked_examples.solution: 1. Calculate the mean: $(3 + 7 + 10 + 14 + 16) / 5 = 50 / 5 = 10$. 2. Determine the median: The data is already ordered. Since there are 5 values (odd), the middle position is the 3rd number, which is 10.

worked_examples.question: Given the data set: 2, 4, 4, 5, 8, 12. Find the range and the interquartile range (IQR).
worked_examples.solution: 1. Range: Subtract the minimum value 2 from the maximum value 12, so $12 - 2 = 10$. 2. IQR: The data is ordered. The lower half is 2, 4, 4, so the median $Q_1 = 4$. The upper half is 5, 8, 12, so the median $Q_3 = 8$. $IQR = Q_3 - Q_1 = 8 - 4 = 4$.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to arrange the data in order from least to greatest before calculating the median.
When there is an even number of values, choosing one of the two middle numbers instead of calculating their average.
Confusing the range (Max - Min) with the interquartile range ($Q_3 - Q_1$).
Incorrectly including or excluding the overall median when calculating $Q_1$ or $Q_3$.
exam_tips: If the problem provides a frequency table, you must multiply each value by its corresponding frequency before summing them to calculate the mean.
The median is more robust (stable) than the mean when dealing with extreme values (outliers).
On the SAT, if a data set is very large, the question usually tests your understanding of definitions rather than requiring tedious calculations.
content.recap: Mean, median, and mode measure the center of the data; range and interquartile range measure the spread. Mastering the definitions and calculation steps for these concepts is key to solving one-variable data problems.

knowledge_claims.content: The mean is calculated by adding all values in a data set and dividing by the total number of values.
The first step in determining the median must be to arrange the data set in order from least to greatest (or greatest to least).
When a data set contains an even number of values, the median is the arithmetic average of the two middle values.
The mode is the value that appears with the highest frequency in a data set.
The formula for the range is the maximum value minus the minimum value.
The first quartile ($Q_1$) is the median of the lower half of an ordered data set.
The third quartile ($Q_3$) is the median of the upper half of an ordered data set.
The formula for the interquartile range (IQR) is $Q_3$ minus $Q_1$.
Compared to the mean, the median is less affected by extreme values (outliers).
The interquartile range measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data.
When calculating the mean from a frequency table, each value must be multiplied by its frequency, summed, and then divided by the sum of the frequencies.
If all values in a data set are identical, both the range and the interquartile range are 0.
